quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: The indemnity package meets our preferred position in full. Section 20.1 gives an unqualified Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims covering Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel, with no Customer-modification or combination carve-outs. Section 20.2 adds Vendor indemnities for breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. Section 20.3 keeps Customer's reverse indemnity narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law), with express carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. Section 20.4 sets balanced procedure (prompt notice with material-prejudice limitation, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, settlement consent protections), and 20.5 provides the procure/modify/replace/refund mitigation remedy without allowing termination of unaffected Services. Indemnification obligations are "Excluded Claims" under 21.3, so they sit outside the mutual cap in 21.1 — better than the 3× super-cap fallback. No redline required.

quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.
rationale: The Agreement already meets our preferred position. §14.2 vests ownership of each Deliverable in Customer upon creation with an express present assignment from Vendor plus personnel assignments and further-assurance cooperation. §14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and pre-existing/independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for Customer; §15.1 reinforces this by barring sale, advertising use, data commingling and model training without our written consent. §14.3 lets Vendor retain only Vendor Technology (defined in §1.8 to exclude Customer Data and Customer's pre-existing IP) and channels embedded Vendor Technology into the §13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify and create derivative works, extended to Affiliates and contractors, with identification and no-restrictive-third-party-material duties. §14.4 negates joint ownership absent a signed instrument and preserves our unrestricted right to use our own feedback. The remaining wrinkles are within our bargaining range and not worth a redline: ownership is conditioned on payment of the applicable Fees (consistent with §10.2's delivery-on-payment mechanic), "Deliverable" is limited to work product an Order Form identifies as created specifically for Customer (curable at Order Form drafting), and the Customer Data definition carves out anonymized telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to us or an individual. Nothing assigns our IP or data to Vendor and no deliverable is owned by Vendor without a licence back, so no walk-away or fallback issue arises.

quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Section 21 delivers the preferred position: 21.1 sets an expressly mutual aggregate cap at the greater of Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve months preceding the claim event and USD 1,000,000; 21.2 excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually while confirming that data restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages; 21.3 defines "Excluded Claims" (uncapped) as breach of confidentiality, data-protection or security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not damages and is not capped; 21.4 preserves liability that cannot lawfully be limited. The cap basis is not illusory: "Fees" (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees. No competing or one-sided liability limitation appears in the warranty (§19), indemnity (§20) or insurance (§18.2, which states insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities) sections.

quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: Section 24 already matches our preferred position. 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only); 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our consent (reasonableness-qualified) and never to a direct competitor; 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control. 24.3 is expressly limited to "other assignments" and so does not swallow the 24.1 carve-out, and its consent standard is mutual and reasonableness-qualified. 13.3 aligns by permitting licence transfer with a Section 24 permitted assignment, and the only other assignment-related termination trigger (9.2 insolvency) carves out lawful reorganizations. No redline needed.

quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
rationale: The grant meets our preferred position. Section 13.1 extends the subscription grant to Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf (plus Authorized Users), and is worldwide and non-exclusive with no "non-transferable" or "revocable" language. Section 13.2 gives Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to paid-up software and Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables, including contractor support rights, and Section 14.3 confirms that licence covers Vendor Technology needed to use a Deliverable. Section 13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor (consistent with the consent-free M&A assignment right in Section 24.1) and limits any revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity, tracking the Section 9.1 cure regime. Section 10.1 preserves paid-up licences after termination. The Section 13.4 restrictions are narrow (no knowing reverse engineering subject to statutory carve-out, no interference or security bypass, no unlawful use) and expressly do not limit authorized security testing or use of Customer Data and output. No redline needed.

quote: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
rationale: Section 9 grants only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and security/SLA/legal-violation (9.3) termination rights; no party has a convenience right. Because Section 8.1 commits us to a three-year term (with 12-month auto-renewals under 8.2), the absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation under the playbook. We therefore add a new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees (leveraging the existing refund mechanics in Section 10.2) and confirm Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a committed term.

Preferred position is no non-solicit on Customer, so we delete § 12.4; fallback (mutual, 12 months, personnel directly involved, with carve-outs and no no-hire) is offered in the comment.

Section 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, and bars withholding data over a fee dispute. Section 11.3 requires secure deletion (active systems and backups as they cycle, with only a legally required copy retained, which stays protected and use-restricted) plus written officer certification. Section 10.1's access cut-off runs only "after any agreed transition period" and expressly preserves Customer Data rights, and Section 16.5 confirms Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15, so the general confidentiality return/destroy provision does not undercut the exit rights. No redline needed.
